prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Generate 5 ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question, each with a short title and a description of one or two sentences. Sample the ideas from the full distribution of possible responses, and give each idea its estimated probability of being generated (a number between 0 and 1).

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and FOS/JUN binding before, during, and long after a transient stimulus (e.g., injury, inflammation, or stress) to test whether AP-1-dependent accessible sites persist after the stimulus is withdrawn and the AP-1 protein itself has returned to baseline.

ideas.title: Secondary challenge (priming) assay with AP-1 perturbation
ideas.description: Expose cells to a first stimulus, rest them, then re-stimulate and measure the faster or stronger transcriptional response. Use inducible dominant-negative AP-1 (A-FOS), CRISPRi, or degron systems at different times to show whether AP-1 is required for establishing versus maintaining the memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing of memory states
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA/ATAC-seq on clonally related cells to determine whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target gene expression states are heritably transmitted through divisions, and whether they predict future response heterogeneity.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporters of AP-1 activity dynamics
ideas.description: Track AP-1 activity using fluorescent reporters or tagged FOS/JUN in single cells over days and across divisions to measure persistence, bistability, and positive feedback (e.g., c-Jun autoregulation), and relate past activity history to current state.

ideas.title: Epigenetic mark and pioneer-factor mechanistic dissection
ideas.description: Combine ChIP/CUT&Tag for histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1), BAF/SWI-SNF recruitment, and DNA methylation with AP-1 motif mutation or site-specific dCas9 editing at memory enhancers to test if AP-1 is necessary and sufficient to establish stable, self-sustaining chromatin states.
